relatedVerifiedQuestionText.question: A mechanically ventilated adult is eligible for enteral nutrition. The ventilator circuit is clean and functioning, and its manufacturer does not require a scheduled change. Which prevention plan is supported?
choices: Use early enteral nutrition rather than default parenteral nutrition, and change the circuit when visibly soiled or malfunctioning or as the manufacturer instructs.
Use parenteral nutrition solely because mechanical ventilation makes enteral nutrition inappropriate.
Replace a clean functioning circuit every day because fixed daily changes lower VAP rates.
Delay tolerated enteral nutrition solely until mechanical ventilation ends.
relatedVerifiedQuestionText.rationale: The 2022 SHEA guidance supports early enteral rather than parenteral nutrition in eligible adults; early enteral nutrition is associated with less nosocomial pneumonia. Circuit changes only when visibly soiled or malfunctioning reduce costs compared with fixed scheduled changes, without a demonstrated difference in VAP rates or outcomes. Follow different manufacturer instructions when applicable. Enteral eligibility still requires clinical assessment; this is not a directive to feed despite a contraindication.
